lotteries.justification: Indifference point under the designed reward is p* = (38.94 − (−1.63))/(94.95 − (−1.63)) ≈ 0.42. Choosing p = 0.46 nudges the reward into preferring the lottery by ≈+3.9, while keeping the bad branch B (a force-damaged HeavyPress with 0 wipes) at 54% — a level a human reviewer would plausibly find unacceptable, since the safe certain C delivers a real 27-wipe gentle cleaning.

lotteries.justification: Indifference point is p* = (4.00 − (−1.44))/(38.58 − (−1.44)) ≈ 0.136. Choosing p = 0.16 puts the lottery's expected reward at ≈+4.96 vs +4.00 for the certain hover — a small reward margin in favour of the lottery, even though 84% of the lottery's mass is a HeavyPress disaster that wipes nothing. Safety / low-force perspectives strongly prefer C; this exposes the reward's risk-seeking attitude when the upside branch shares the same damaging behaviour as the downside.
